posts.title: AWS Emulator and the engineer's job when agents write the code
posts.description: AWS Emulator, launched today and written and tested entirely by agents, gives you a local copy of more than 200 AWS services to test against. Swami Sivasubramanian recalls the high-fidelity simulation his team built to test one of Amazon's earliest distributed systems, and writes about how the engineer's work changes when agents write the code.

posts.title: The oldest architecture in computing
posts.description: A GPU burns 700 watts and hundreds of thousands of tries to learn Pong. A human brain does it on 20 watts in a handful of attempts. So what can the oldest architecture in computing teach us about where agents and memory are headed?

posts.title: DuckDB and the changing physics of analytics
posts.description: In this post, Andy Warfield explains how databases like DuckDB are enabling a new way to build with data, why they matter right now, and how they complement the work we’ve been doing in S3 (e.g., S3 Files, S3 Tables, S3 Vectors). And most importantly, why DuckLabs, the team behind DuckDB, is joining AWS
